notes: No tables in this chapter, so 'text vs table' checks were run against the tables in the source chapters (trace-eda, twopool, predictors, closedloop, validation, baselines) that the intro restates. The only numeric recomputation that outright fails is the 1.1% live-anchor lower bound (finding 1), which is a rounding defect inherited from validation.tex rather than originated here. The remaining findings are definitional: the chapter uses two different denominators for its single headline cost ratio ('deployable static' at L50/271/481/514 vs 'best static' at L211 and 'best static configuration' at L260) and two different spans for the same pricing ('the covered week' at L50 vs '5.60-day covered span' at L270). Both are cheap to fix and both propagate to the conclusion and the abstract. Two derived observations that are NOT defects but a reviewer may raise: (a) 2.7% of requests carrying 81.2% of image volume implies a per-request image-count ratio of (81.2/2.7)/(18.8/97.3) = 155.6x between the frames and non-frames classes, not the ~140x an approximate reading suggests; (b) the intro consistently writes the zero-queueing service floor as 588 ms, which matches closedloop's tab:cl-aggregate, while closedloop's tab:cl-ewma writes 589 ms for what reads as the same floor - the intro picked one side of a discrepancy internal to closedloop, so the fix belongs there. Footnote microbenchmarks (3--5 s readiness, 1.15 GB / 0.11 s / 0.13 s checkpoint load) and the model-architecture facts (576M tower, 4096-d and 5120-d projectors) contain no internal relation to recompute against; the only checkable one, 5120/4096 = 5/4, passes.
